problem: Given that $L{t\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{2\omega s}{({s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2})^{2}},$ find the Laplace transform $L{{e}^{3t}\cdot t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)}.$
worked_solution:
The first shifting theorem states that if
$L{f(t)}=F(s),$
then
$L{{e}^{at}f(t)}=F(s-a).$

Using the given result, we have

$$
L{t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)}=\frac{2(5)s}{({s}^{2}+{5}^{2})^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, applying the first shifting theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{3t}\cdot t\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)} & =\frac{2(5)(s-3)}{((s-3)^{2}+{5}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10(s-3)}{((s-3)^{2}+25)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
